headline: Approved minutes, vendor payments, and roof replacement; discussed irrigation, capital projects, and course issues
summary: The commission approved the July 14, 2026 minutes and several vendor invoices for repairs including a water pump, dishwasher, sink hole repair, and plumber support. It also approved replacing the roof over the heat plant. The group discussed ongoing projects such as cart path patching, a tennis wind screen, hole 16 tee screening, a water station for golfers, a clubhouse renovation, and a golf course irrigation system costing an estimated $3 million, with no final decisions made on these items.
decisions: Approved payment to ARC Mechanical for a new water pump due to a cooling issue.
Approved payment to Summit Supply for dishwasher repair.
Approved payment to Amrize Hot Top Co. for repair of McKay Street due to a sink hole at the pump house area.
Approved payment to F.W. Webb Co., Drainpro/Spenseer for plumber support in the clubhouse sink.
Approved replacing the roof over the heat plant.

# MEETING MINUTES

*Received and recorded: City of Beverly, City Clerk's Office, 2026 SEP 17 P 12:21*

- **Board:** Golf and Tennis Commission
- **Date:** August 11,2026
- **Location:** Beverly Golf & Tennis
- **Members Present:** Chair William Lowd, Vice-Chair Martin Lawler, Arthur Athanas, Chad Crandall, Kevin Ascolillo, Paul Sciamanna
- **Guests:** Chris Carter, Sean Ciancarellli, Steve Murphy, Mike LaPierre, Jim Tognazzi, Bryant Ayles, David Gelineau
- **Recorder:** Donna Musumeci

## Minutes

Chad Crandall: Motion to approve the minutes of July 14, 2026. Martin Lawler seconded. The motion carries (6-0).

## Financial Updates: Martin Lawler

Bryant Ayles joined the finance discussion. Bryant advised FY26 balance from this year, which will go back to the vault. He will verify this. He did confirm that $400K is approved for the 2027 budget, plus the balance from what is left from FY26, (budget will need to be approved by the city council).

Commission reviewed invoices from multiple vendors:

- **ARC Mechanical** - New water pump, cooling issue. Arthur Athanas: Motion to approve, Kevin Ascolillo seconded. The motion carries (6-0).
- **Summit Supply** - Dishwasher repair. Arthur Athanas: Motion to pay, Kevin Ascolillo seconded. The motion carries (6-0).
- **Amrize Hot Top Co.** - Repair of McKay Street due to sink hole at pump house area. Arthur Athanas: Motion to pay, Kevin Ascolillo and Paul Sciamanna seconded. Motion carries (6-0).
- **F.W. Webb Co., Drainpro/Spenseer** - Plumber support in Clubhouse sink. Arthur Athanas: Motion to pay, Kevin Ascolillo seconded. The motion carries (6-0).

## Site Projects / Status / Discussions & Updates

**Rennick Family clock** - The clock is installed and working. Steve commented it was quite a project, but it lights up now, and the location works well. Arthur said it was all very well done, in addition to the family raising money.

Dino Paving Co. has been hired to patch cart paths; work will be done when it gets scheduled (TBD).

Greenjacket Covers for the greens, ordered, have not arrived yet. Oval tennis wind screen has been installed at Tennis Courts.

**Hole 16 TEE** - want something in place so onlookers from street cannot distract golfer. Jim advised we can buy a green mesh construction screen and zip tie it to the fence. It is very durable; he will get a price. Chris recommended using plastic slats which are durable, and not permanent but work much better. Jim will get a quote. We will address it again at the next meeting.

Bill discussed a complaint from a golfer about no water on the course. Consulted with the Board of Health. Chris advised that down the line, a water line could be installed. Another option could be a touchless fountain water station recommended for the back nine. In the meantime, golfers must bring/use their water bottle.

Roof over the heat plant work to be done, quotes to be reviewed. Athur Athanas: Motion to replace the roof over the heat plant. Paul Sciamanna seconded. The motion carries (6-0).

**Bridge/Culvert Hole 8/9** - Sean and Jim plan to install a safety rail for the bridge between hole 8 and 9. They will use big timbers to create a safety rail: Schedule pending.

## Capital Projects

Bill went to Jerry Sullivan, previously involved with clubhouse renovation project, and asked him to go back into the plan looking at the windows. The architects quote estimate is to do the windows as a whole package. It would of course, have to go out to bid. Bill will ask them to come out to take another look at maybe doing it in phases or by floors. Needs further discussion.

Irrigation of the golf course. Steve Murphy talked to White Engineering, who did the pump station. Will want to get a system that could last 30 years to replacing the sprinkler system. Doing the new piping should last 100 years. Preliminary estimate for a new system is $3 million. Today the heads keep breaking etc., quote from White Engineering is $35K to design it. Bryant advised this could be done in a month as far as funding it. If you are going to pay $35K for the design, you should know how you plan to pay for it. Bryant says you are getting more expenses at the golf course. Bryant said there are competing priorities for the building, versus an irrigation system. Dave advised us to think of more ways to support spending this money, i.e., do membership fees go up, maybe green fees increase? Chris advised fees have not gone up in 5 years, but we are due to do it next year. Suggestion is to create multiple funding avenues. Bryant said to lay out prioritization with the group, he recommends we do an exercise as a group.

Chad asked Bryant if he can explain the debt and bond to us? Bryant advised he will present an amortization table so we can see what we can afford. Chad said it is a combo of fees, grants, plus the loans. Chad said it would be great to generate more revenue in the clubhouse.

**Hole 18** - Dave said BSC has done 2 sets of drawings, one set for 1st tee, we must go back to the conservation commission and have a conversation. Where do we stand with Tibbetts? Dave said it could lead to litigation.

Steve discussed John's project on the 8th tee. (John was a guest at the meeting). John commented that markings that were done on the penalty areas are noticeably clear and hopes it can be maintained. He recommended tree management be done and said it can be impactful for golf. Athur asked for examples to be sent. One was on hole fifteen, when standing on the tee, you cannot see half of the green.

## GFMI Update

Chris Carter advised July numbers were slightly under 7769 rounds, there were a few rain outs in July. Expect similar performance for August and September.

Revenue report - under what we expected, will result in higher green fees, will be looking at the membership list, and revenue at the 19th hole.

Chris thanked Jim T. for always being responsive, advised invoice coming from Secure Lock and Alarm for Door closure on Pub door, and supply and install a new lever on the cart building.

Arthur Athanas: Motion to adjourn, Kevin Asolillo seconded. The motion carries (6-0).
